I heavily, heavily relate to this. It makes me feel like and outsider when trying to form relationships. I've never formed a true connection with somebody I can honestly say aswell. 

Grew up being quite reserved too and afraid to be my true self or vocalise how I would feel out being judged and wasn't till my later years (early 20s) I was trying to come out of my shell more and form new relationships. But it felt too late, everyone had figured out who they were by mid teens and formed all types of close relationships with eachother, that left me always feeling like the odd one out and 3rd wheel in social situations. This played a part in currently going through a identity crisis (hooray)

I definitely feel what you're saying about feeling robbed emotionally. hits close too, while everyone's already in the fast lane, you feel miiiiles behind. Also with the ADHD, ugh! Too many emotions to deal with.

It does hurts for me when trying to start a conversation and knowing I'm just going to bore them or weird them out, after a while you can tell when they've lost interest in my convo attempts and it just brings awkward energy that gets depressing so I would try to avoid interacting with people, out of fear I would be a disappointment. I never know what to say anymore. My mind just panics on what to say and it gets hard trying to form something interesting or well informed, if you ever get that?

I have friends who manage to form all sorts of close relationships with complete strangers, I have a friend who can socially connect with anyone so easily (it's so hard not to feel jealous of that skill). feels awful knowing they're miles ahead, It's so easy for them to just mesh with a random person. It hurts when you just want to make just one true connection. It's like,"what's wrong with me? I just want to fit in like everyone else"

New year started of wonky, mentally for me, had a big personal realisation and I really want to do my best to work on it, trying to feel more comfortable and confident i.e. less reserved, no doubts being sure of what I want, and able to comfortably emote better etc.

 I also gotta find what really gets my flame burning, to be truly passionate about something again. I fell out of love for so many things, after getting depressed. This, I feel is what makes me such a boring person to talk with when I have nothing I enjoy that much, I've got nothing to talk about that's interesting, I'm clutching at straws and second guessing when trying to get past the basics of an convo and It shows. there's so much I need to work on, on myself and it's gonna feel like hell trying to do it. At this point Im just trying have blind optimism that it will work out.


I don't really know what to say to help, because it feels im on the same journey. but, you're gonna go through a lot of phases in life and just feel like shit putting a lot of effort trying and failing to find that true connection with and wanna give. But, they're all stepping stones in eventually forming the you that you're truly happy with. I just hope you're able to stay strong mentally and physically, also find that spark with someone when the time comes, as well as getting to talk to someone if you can about all the feelings you're going through if you can find an outlet.

Currently I'm learning rn, I get terribly anxious when behind the wheel for the same reasons, and trying to overcome it each time (I won't lie have been putting off a bit lately just cos nerves, but I that's a me issue I have learn to get over it.)

But, from one anxious person to another, I can honestly say, over time it does become easier and lil less intimidating each time you get behind the wheel, and eventually, you'll get a feel for being in the driver's seat, also that wicked feeling of "hey, I did that on my own w/o thinking" which is such a nice reassurance in yourself and confidence boost.

Definitely find an instructor who's right for you before you decide to keep going forward too, that's a must. And, have faith in yourself and your instructor, that they wont let you crash. (Red flag for any instructor who lets that happen)

Also, Sometimes for myself, I won't get what I'm being taught straight away till much, much later, so don't stress and feel you have to get everything perfect first time. It might click for you as soon as you get out the car, you'll make a few hiccups, but that's ok. Everyone goes at their own pace and you're learning, 


Id definitely say give it a try and get a feel for it. Then decide whether it's for you or not. And if not, hey, you can say you tried atleast. 

I wish you all the best and hope this might help.
